The surah opens in the manner of an army launching an attack: there is no preamble and no introduction. A decree is announced that the deeds of those who disbelieve, who bar others and themselves from the path of Allah, are nullified. The announcement is made in a highly effective, easily understood and concrete manner. Their deeds have lost their way and, as a result, have been destroyed and wasted, as though they were living humans or animals that have strayed, gone far off and perished. This meaning and this picture convey that these deeds have become detached from their people, as a flock of cattle becomes separated from its herd, and that both the people and their deeds have ended in ruin.

The announcement that these deeds are lost takes the form of a military decree. The deeds of goodness referred to here are those deprived of faith and of the spirit of jihad, whose doers intend mere goodness. Therefore, the value of righteous deeds lies in nothing other than faith and the ideology of jihad, because deeds of this kind, which outwardly appear to be good deeds, lack a driving motive of goodness at their core. Sometimes the motive is indeed one of goodness, but it is not rooted in faith. Thus, without faith, there is a temporary and superficial impulse, which causes certain deeds to be performed, but they lack stability and permanence; they are not based on any firm and clear method or ideology, and they lie outside the long-term plan of life. They are not connected to the hidden order of Allah within this universe, and therefore they are null. Hence faith is necessary for deeds, so that they may be bound to it and proceed in a correct direction, and the doer may act from that faith-based motive, and this deed may also be connected to that cosmic system which joins man to this universe. In this way, every deed in this universe has a purpose and an effect, and it reaches a destination.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 47, verse 2:

And on the other hand:

"And those who believe and do righteous deeds and accept what has been sent down upon Muhammad (ﷺ), and it is the truth from their Lord" (47:2).

In "those who believe" (alladhina amanu) belief in Muhammad (ﷺ) is included, but here it is mentioned separately as an emphasis, so that this statement may be brought as its attribute.

"And it is the truth from their Lord" (wa huwa al-haqq min rabbihim): this further reinforces the earlier belief, and the performance of righteous deeds is a sign that faith is alive, present and active.

"Allah has removed their evil deeds from them" (kaffara 'anhum sayyi'atahum): this is the predicate of "those who". The deeds of the disbelievers had been rendered void, although those deeds appeared to be good. Their lack of faith and the existence of disbelief caused them to be voided, whereas the evil deeds of the believers were also removed and they were forgiven. This is a complete contrast: through disbelief good deeds are lost, and through faith evil deeds are erased. This is the significance of faith.

"And He has set right their state" (wa aslaha balahum): setting right someone's state is a great blessing, which comes as a result and effect of faith. Prosperity and peace of mind are a manifestation of tranquility, contentment, and the pleasure and peace of Allah. When a person is inwardly content, his consciousness, his thought, his heart, his conscience, his ideas, his nerves and his whole self function in the best possible manner, and he lives a life of peace and security. There is no greater blessing than the tranquility of the heart. It is a horizon that is most luminous and clear and transparent, and access to it is granted only to the people of faith.

That He has annulled the deeds of the disbelievers and pardoned the evil deeds of the believers is not based on friendship or kinship, nor is it merely by chance; rather, it was done according to an effective and determined principle, in accordance with the law of nature upon which this universe is established. This law is truth, which is the foundation of creation, and according to which Allah created the heavens and the earth.

"That is because those who disbelieve follow falsehood, and those who believe follow the truth from their Lord." As for falsehood, its roots do not extend deep into this universe, so it perishes; and whoever follows falsehood or is a product of falsehood is bound to be lost. And since the disbelievers are followers of falsehood, their deeds are lost, and nothing beneficial of theirs remains. And since truth is enduring, and the heavens and the earth are established upon it, its roots extend far into this universe. Therefore it remains, and since believers are its followers, they too are granted permanence, and Allah overlooks their shortcomings and sets their condition right.

This is a clear and settled matter, founded on fixed principles and definite causes; therefore there is nothing accidental in it, nor is it based merely on chance.

﴿Thus does Allah set forth for people their examples﴾ (47:3). That is, Allah tells people the principles by which they should weigh themselves and their deeds, and the standards by which they should conduct their affairs; they are not free to devise their own measures and scales.

Having established this principle in the previous verse, the believers are then given guidance to prepare for battle, because they are followers of the truth, and the establishment and dominance of this truth on this earth is necessary. Dominance is in the nature of truth. It is truth that is to set the standards of people's lives, and to shape people's lives according to its principles; and since the disbelievers are upon falsehood, the traces of both falsehood and its people must necessarily be erased.

The verse speaks of meeting the disbelievers in the sense of actual combat, not mere encounter. Until this surah was revealed, some people in the Arabian Peninsula were at war with the Muslims and others had treaties of peace with them. Surah al-Bara'ah had not yet been revealed, and it was that surah which brought the treaties with the polytheists to an end. The ruling was that treaties with a fixed term would remain in force until their term expired, and those without a fixed term were given a period of four months. It was also ordered that after this, any polytheist found anywhere in the Arabian Peninsula would be killed, because the Arabian Peninsula was the centre of Islam and had to be reserved exclusively for the Muslims. In the Arabian Peninsula, polytheists had to either accept Islam or be expelled from the land. This principle does not apply to other regions. In other Islamic lands, polytheists may live as a minority by paying the jizya (poll tax). Moreover, the command to strike necks applies only when they do not accept Islam. Striking necks is the practical form of killing, and it suits the atmosphere of this surah.

﴿Until, when you have thoroughly subdued them, then bind them firmly﴾ (47:4). Ithkhan (subduing thoroughly) means to inflict severe slaughter, that is, to crush the enemy. It means to break the enemy's power so that it has no capacity left to attack. Only when the enemy has reached that position should the taking of captives begin. But if the enemy's head has not been crushed, the taking of captives should not begin.

According to this exegesis, there will be no contradiction between this verse and the verse of al-Anfal in which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims were rebuked for taking many people captive at the Battle of Badr, when it was proper that they be killed, as some exegetes have understood. In Surah al-Anfal it is said:

﴿It is not for a Prophet to have captives until he has thoroughly subdued the land. You desire the goods of this world, but Allah desires the Hereafter, and Allah is Mighty and Wise. Had there not been a decree from Allah already written, a great punishment would have touched you for what you took﴾ (8:67-68).

Therefore, crushing the enemy's power comes first, so that the enemy cannot attack the Islamic state in future, and only after that does the matter of captivity arise. The purpose of war is precisely to eliminate the force that attacks the Islamic state. This is especially so in circumstances where the number of Muslims is small and the polytheists are numerous. In the warfare of that era, eliminating the enemy's soldiers was of great importance in military strategy. This same ruling will remain in force even now, if the objective depends on it, that is, if the enemy's power cannot be crushed without severe slaughter and the enemy cannot be prevented from attacking again without it. After this, the command to take captives applies, and this is the only explicit text that determines the rule concerning captives.

﴿Then either grant them release as a favour, or take ransom﴾ (47:4). That is, with regard to prisoners of war, after the enemy has been subdued, you have the choice either to release them as a favour or to deal with them by ransom. That is, you may release them for the ransom of Muslim captives, or accept some financial compensation for war, or take some other service in return. This is what was done with some of the captives of Badr.

This verse provides no third option for the disposal of captives. That is, it does not permit killing them or enslaving them, in the case of polytheist captives. However, in practice, afterwards, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the caliphs did enslave some captives and killed some under specific circumstances.

For the explanation of this verse, I quote the explanation of Imam al-Jassas al-Hanafi. Where I have something to say, I will say it in between, and after that I will state the meaning which, in my view, is correct. Al-Jassas says:

"Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So when you meet those who disbelieve, strike necks﴾ (47:4). The apparent meaning of the verse requires that any other treatment of the disbelievers is permissible only after their power has been thoroughly crushed. A similar ruling appears elsewhere: ﴿It is not permissible for a Prophet to have captives until he has thoroughly subdued the enemy in the land﴾ (8:67). (And this is correct, because there is no contradiction between the two verses (Qutb)."

Ibn Jafar Muhammad ibn al-Hakam narrated from Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Yaman, from Abu Ubayd, from Abdullah ibn Salih, from Muawiyah ibn Salih, from Ali ibn Talhah, and he from Ibn Abbas, that the verse ﴿It is not for a Prophet...in the land﴾ (8:67) concerns the Day of Badr. At that time the Muslims were few. When they became many and their power increased, Allah sent down the second verse: ﴿Then either grant them release as a favour, or take ransom﴾ (47:4). Allah gave the Prophet and the Muslims the choice: if they wished, they could kill, if they wished, they could enslave, and if they wished, they could take ransom. Abu Ubayd expressed doubt about these words ("if they wished, they could enslave"). Since enslavement is itself doubtful as a report from Ibn Abbas, we set it aside. As for killing, the verse does not show its permissibility, because the verse is explicit about granting release as a favour or releasing for ransom.

Jafar ibn Muhammad narrated from Abu Ubayd, from Abu Mahdi and Hajjaj, both from Sufyan, who said that he heard Suddi explain this verse: ﴿Then either grant them release as a favour, or take ransom﴾ (47:4), and that this verse was abrogated by the verse of Surah al-Tawbah: ﴿Kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ (9:5). Abu Bakr al-Jassas says that this verse ﴿So when you meet those who disbelieve, strike necks﴾ (47:4), and the verse ﴿It is not for a Prophet...in the land﴾ (8:67), and the verse ﴿If you overtake them in war, then disperse those behind them﴾ (8:57), all these rulings can remain established and need not be abrogated. This is because Allah commanded the Prophet (ﷺ) to kill the polytheists thoroughly and not to take captives, unless they were completely humiliated and their power was broken. That was when the number of Muslims was small. Therefore it is appropriate that this command remain in force and be acted upon in circumstances like the early days of Islam. (My view is that the command to kill polytheists wherever they are found was only for the polytheists of the Arabian Peninsula, whereas this verse under discussion is general.) When the enemy's power has been crushed, then taking captives becomes permissible. The caliphs acted upon this after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and it was also acted upon after the revelation of Surah al-Bara'ah. They did not kill any captive except in certain specific circumstances.

As for the verse ﴿Then either grant them release as a favour, or take ransom﴾ (47:4), the apparent meaning of the phrase is that you may do one of two things: either release the captives as a favour, or release them for ransom. This negates the permissibility of killing captives. The righteous predecessors (salaf al-salihin) differed on this. It is reported that Hajjaj ibn al-Mubarak, from Ibn Fudalah, from Hasan, disliked killing a captive, and [...] he treated him kindly, dealing with him by ransom. Jafar narrated to us from Abu Ubayd, from Hashim, from Ash'ath, that I asked Ata about the ruling on killing a captive, and he said: either release him as a favour or deal with him by ransom. I asked Hasan the same question and he said: he should be treated as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) treated the captives of Badr, that is, either released as a favour or ransomed. It is reported from Ibn Umar that a leader of the notables of Istakhr was handed over to him as a captive so that he might kill him, but he refused to kill him and recited this verse: ﴿Then either grant them release as a favour, or take ransom﴾ (47:4). Similarly, Mujahid and Muhammad ibn Sirin also reported this, and they disliked the killing of captives. It is reported from Suddi that this verse ﴿Then either grant them release as a favour, or take ransom﴾ (47:4) was abrogated by ﴿Kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ (9:5). A similar report is also transmitted from Ibn Jurayj. Jafar narrated, from Abu Ubayd, from Hajjaj, and from Ibn Jurayj, who said that this verse is abrogated. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt bound and killed on the day of Badr. Nadr ibn al-Harith was also killed on the day of Badr, and on the day of Uhud, Abu Azzah the poet was killed after being taken captive. Banu Qurayzah was also put to death when they surrendered after accepting the judgement of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, who ruled that they should be killed and their children enslaved. Of them, only Zubayr ibn Bata was shown mercy. Part of Khaybar was conquered by treaty and part by force. With Abu al-Huqayq there was a condition that he would conceal nothing. When it became clear that he had concealed something, he was killed.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) conquered Makkah and ordered that Bilal ibn Fatal, Mutays ibn Hababah, Abdullah ibn Abi al-Sarh and others be killed. He said: "Even if they are clinging to the curtains of the Ka'bah, kill them." He showed kindness to the people of Makkah and did not make their property spoils of war. It is reported from Salih ibn Kaysan, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, from his father Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, that he heard Abu Bakr al-Siddiq say: "I wish that when Fujaah was brought to me, I had not burned him, and had either killed him freely or released him successfully." Abu Musa killed a landowner of al-Sus after giving him protection. What happened was that he was given assurance that certain people would not be killed, but in that agreement he forgot to write his name, and so he was killed. These are the traditions and reports which have come down through the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Companions by mass transmission, that captives may be kept and may also be killed, and the jurists of the major cities agree on this. (The permissibility of this killing is not derived from the verse, but only from the practice of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and some Companions.) However, if the circumstances in which captives were killed are studied in detail, it becomes evident that those who were killed had specific reasons for their killing. These reasons were in addition to war and to being taken captive. Nadr ibn al-Harith and Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt used to satirise the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Makkah and tormented him and those who carried the call of Islam. The same was the case with Abu Azzah the poet. As for Banu Qurayzah, they had already accepted the judgement of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh in advance. In short, in all these situations, specific causes are apparent. Therefore, in these circumstances, action was taken apart from this verse, that is, apart from the words "favour" and "ransom").

Regarding the release of captives in return for ransom, there was also disagreement. Our companions (the Hanafis) are all of the view that captives should not be released in exchange for property, and that captive slaves should not be sold to anyone in the Abode of War so that they may fight against Islam again. The opinion of Imam Abu Hanifah is that such captives should not be released even in exchange for Muslim captives, so that they can never wage war against Islam. Imam Yusuf and Imam Muhammad say that polytheist captives may be exchanged for Muslim captives. This is also the opinion of Imam al-Thawri and Imam al-Awza'i. Imam al-Awza'i said that women and children may also be sold to the people of the Abode of War. However, adult male slaves should not be sold. Imam al-Muzani reported from Imam al-Shafi'i that the leader (imam) has the choice either to release them as a favour or to release them for ransom. Those who do not permit releasing disbelieving captives in exchange for property or for Muslim captives have this as their evidence:

﴿Then either grant them release as a favour, or take ransom﴾ (47:4). The apparent words of the verse give the meaning that release in exchange for property or in exchange for Muslim captives is permissible. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) released the men of Badr in exchange for property. The argument for release in exchange for property is drawn from the hadith narrated by Ibn al-Mubarak from Ma'mar, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu al-Muhallab, and from Imran ibn Husayn: that the tribe of Thaqif had taken two companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) captive, and the Muslims had taken a man from the tribe of Banu Amir ibn Sa'sa'ah captive. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by this captive, who was bound. He called out to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), asking what his offence was. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You have been seized because of the crime of your companions." The captive said: "I am a Muslim." Upon hearing this, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If you had said this when you were free, you would have been completely successful." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) left. The captive called out again, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned to him. He said: "I am hungry." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Yes, this is your need." After that, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) released him in exchange for the two Muslims whom Thaqif had taken captive. (In our view, the arguments of those who hold that captives may be released by ransom are strong, compared with the arguments Imam al-Jassas has given against ransom in property or the exchange for Muslim captives.)

Imam al-Jassas concluded his discussion by preferring the opinion of the Hanafis. He said that because the verse under discussion mentions favour and ransom, this verse has been abrogated by the following verse:

﴿Kill the polytheists wherever you find them, and seize them, and besiege them, and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush. Then if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakah, let them go their way﴾ (9:5). This is the same report that we have transmitted from Suddi and Ibn Jurayj. And the saying of Allah...

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 47, verse 4 (part 2 of 2):

﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah and the Last Day, and do not forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, and do not follow the religion of truth, from among those who were given the Scripture, until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled﴾ (9:29).

The ruling of both verses is that you should fight the disbelievers until they pay the jizyah, and any ransom, whether in wealth or otherwise, is contrary to this. The people of tafsir and the Companions' followers (tabi'un) through their reports agree that Surah al-Tawbah was revealed after Surah Muhammad. Therefore the ruling of Surah al-Tawbah will abrogate (naskh) the ruling that is in Surah Muhammad. (Earlier we have said that the ruling that the polytheists will either be killed or accept Islam applies only to the polytheists of Makkah; it is a ruling specific to them. As for the non-polytheist Arabs, it is permissible to accept jizyah from them, as it is from the People of the Book; and before accepting jizyah, these people may become captives in the hands of the Muslims. The question is: when they may become captives before jizyah is accepted, what are the rulings concerning those captives? We say: the Imam may show them grace, may take ransom wealth, and may also exchange them for prisoners, if their people remain strong and do not accept jizyah. If they accept jizyah, then they will be released. That is a different situation. Therefore, as long as the disbelievers do not accept jizyah, the ruling of the verse under discussion continues to apply.)

The summary of the matter is this: this is the only Qur'anic verse that states the ruling on captives, and the other verse does not relate to this subject. Therefore, in the matter of captives, this verse shall be regarded as the primary source of law, and the events that occurred contrary to it took place in particular circumstances, which were temporary circumstances. Some captives were killed because of their other individual crimes, and such situations may possibly arise again in the future. They were seized because of deeds and crimes that preceded their captivity; it is not merely because of being at war and being captives. For example, if a person is caught in espionage, he will not be considered a prisoner of war but a spy. This detention is only to keep the criminal in custody.

As for the matter of enslaving captives, at that time it was an international issue. We have discussed it repeatedly in Zilal al-Quran. It was a common military strategy of that time. Therefore Islam could, at that time, act upon it unilaterally in every situation, namely upon "either grace afterwards or ransom" (47:4 in the Arabic numbering used here: fa-imma mannan ba'du wa-imma fida'). While the enemies of Islam were taking Muslims captive and enslaving them, the Messenger ﷺ in some circumstances enslaved war captives, in some circumstances released captives out of grace, in some exchanged captives for ransom, and from some he took financial compensation; and in some circumstances war captives were also enslaved, because these decisions and measures were in accordance with the international law of that time and were necessary.

If it happens somewhere (and in our era it has happened) that all international powers decide not to enslave captives, then at that time Islam too will return to that positive principle, which is: "either grace afterwards or ransom" (47:4), that is, either the captives are released as a favour, or released against ransom, so that the circumstances in which captives were enslaved are brought to an end, because in Islam the institution of slavery is not necessary and is not a fundamental principle.

This is the opinion that is definitively known from the explicit Qur'anic text, and it is also indicated by all those circumstances and events that emerged in the early period of Islam. And the correct opinion is the one to which Allah grants someone success. But it should be kept well in mind that this opinion is established from the Qur'anic texts at first sight, and the events and circumstances of the early centuries also indicate the same; it is not the case that someone has accused Islam of permitting the institution of slavery, and I deny this and defend Islam. I do not subscribe to this kind of defence. If my view were that Islam considers slavery permissible, I would announce that this is correct and that the good of humanity lies in keeping the institution of slavery permitted; and no human being who is human and who has even a little awareness of Islamic manners could say that the Qur'an says this, but my opinion is different, and my opinion is more reasonable than the Qur'an.

These laws and directives, namely fighting, striking necks, binding captives firmly, and these principles regarding captives, remain in force until:

﴿until the war lays down its burdens﴾ (47:4), and the struggle between Islam and its enemies comes to an end. This is a general principle, and jihad is an institution that continues until the Day of Resurrection, just as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Until the word of Allah is the highest," that is, until the word of Allah becomes supreme.

* * *

Allah did not prescribe this jihad because He wants help from people against the disbelievers. Allah can destroy the disbelievers directly. This system has been prescribed so that Allah may test some of His servants by means of others. Their ranks in the Hereafter will be decided on the basis of this trial.

﴿That, and if Allah had willed, He would have avenged Himself upon them; but [He ordained fighting] to test some of you by means of others. And those who are killed in the way of Allah — He will never waste their deeds. He will guide them and amend their condition, and admit them to Paradise which He has made known to them﴾ (47:4–6).

Those who disbelieved and barred others from the way of Allah are found in every age and place: rebels against the religion of God, insolent and corrupt people who appear in the garb of oppression and arrogance and show themselves and their followers as very powerful. They are a handful of people, and they live upon that tiny speck which is commonly called the earth, which in fact is only a speck among the great spheres, giant bodies, stars and planets of this universe. Beyond it are other worlds, countless galaxies and black holes, whose number only Allah knows, and which float and scatter through this vast and awesome universe. In comparison with them, this earth is merely a speck, a tiny grain of mustard seed. This terrifying order and arrangement of all these worlds has been established by Allah alone. Therefore the owner of all powers is Allah alone.

These dictators of the world and their followers, indeed this whole earth and its entire population, in relation to this universe, are like a hive of extremely tiny ants of some ten or twelve billion in relation to the people of the earth; indeed, if this relation were expressed by the arithmetical rule of proportion (earth : universe = earth : speck), it would not even be that. The whole earth and its population, compared with the universe, are less than a speck. And the powers of Allah are even wider than the universe. La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah!

Allah commands the believers: strike the necks of these enemies of Islam, and bind them firmly after thoroughly subduing them. These commands have been given so that the believers may become instruments in the hand of divine power. If Allah willed, He would take revenge upon the disbelievers directly and openly, just as He destroyed some peoples through storms, thunderous cries, and winds that annihilate; indeed, Allah can take vengeance even without these means, by His command "Be" and it is. But Allah desires good for His believing servants; He tests them, trains them, reforms them, and provides them with the means of good deeds.

Allah tests the believers, and in this trial He stirs the finest sentiments in the hearts of the believers. And what finer sentiment could there be than that a person's creed becomes dearer to him than his own life, so that he struggles for that cherished creed, fights, kills and is killed; and his condition is such that he makes no compromise or tolerance in matters of religion, cannot live without that religion, and cannot live according to any other way than that religion.

And Allah trains the believers in such a way that He removes from their hearts all the desires and all the inclinations of this transient world, although it is very difficult for a human being to remove such desires from the heart. Thus weakness is removed from their hearts, defect is transformed into perfection, and every kind of alloy is expelled. To the extent that if all their desires were placed in one pan of a scale, and in the other pan were only the call to jihad and the seeking of Allah's pleasure, then the pan of Allah's pleasure and jihad would be found heavier. Allah makes it manifest that when these souls were given the choice they chose the religion; when they were trained they recognised the truth; and they do not take a step without thought, but take steps after careful consideration.

And Allah wishes to reform the believers: through jihad in the way of Allah, and through repeatedly facing Allah's hardships and death, the fear of death itself is removed from their minds. Whereas people remove the fear of death from their souls, their morals and their values only after great effort, and by enduring great hardships; but the person who is a mujahid in the way of Allah keeps facing death at all times and becomes accustomed to it. Whether he encounters death or escapes it, the thought and resolve to die in the way of Allah, especially in moments of extreme danger, sends a current like electricity through the human body; and whoever emerges safely from such stages comes with a renewed spirit and a pure and clean personality. The personality of the one who takes part in jihad, that is, the ghazi, is indeed unique.

Furthermore, this jihad is a means of reforming the whole human community: when leadership of humanity comes into the hands of those mujahideen whose souls are pure of all worldly defilements and filth, and in whose eyes all the glittering things of the world are worthless, indeed they consider even this whole worldly life contemptible, when they leap into the wells of death. No thing of the world, no allurement, can draw their gaze towards itself, and they seek only the pleasure of God. When the leadership of the world is in the hands of such people, people are reformed and the world too is reformed; corruption and disorder come to an end and the world takes refuge in the embrace of peace and security, because they have obtained these lofty aims at the price of their own blood, and they have obtained them not for personal interests but for the pleasure of Allah.

Then this is the grace and facilitation of Allah, which He grants to whichever fortunate person He wills, so that he may gather Allah's mercies without measure. And for those who are eternally wretched, a path is also made available by Allah, as a result of which they receive His wrath and punishment; "every one We assist with the provision of your Lord" (17:20). And whoever among the righteous receives this share, and Allah gives it only to one whose inner self is prepared for it. It has been stated what the end is for those who are killed or who kill in the way of Allah.

﴿And those who are killed in the way of Allah — never will He waste their deeds﴾ (47:4).

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 47, verse 5:

﴿He will guide them and set their condition right﴾ (48:5), ﴿and admit them into the Garden which He has made known to them﴾ (48:6). ﴿He will guide them and set their state right and admit them into Paradise, of which He has informed them.﴾ He will not let their deeds go to waste. This is in contrast to what was said about the disbelievers, that their deeds would be lost. The reason is that the deeds of the believers are firmly rooted in the true root, and that root is the tree of truth. These deeds issue forth from that truth. They are in support of the truth and in the direction of the truth. Therefore they endure and possess the quality of permanence, because the truth is everlasting.

The reality of the martyrs (shuhada', witnesses who die in the cause of God) deserves reflection. God has given His judgment about them in another place: ﴿And do not say of those who are killed in the way of God, "They are dead." Rather, they are alive, but you do not perceive﴾. But here they are presented from another aspect: that in the path in which they sacrificed the enjoyment of their lives, they are continuously moving forward. That path is the path of guidance, sincerity, purity and obedience.

﴿He will guide them and set their state right﴾ (47:5): God guides them. They were killed in the way of their Lord, Allah, and He still guides them. That is, even after martyrdom they are traversing exalted stages, their conditions are being set right, and their souls are being purified from the defilements of the earth. The station they hold in the Exalted Assembly (al-Mala' al-A'la, the angelic host of the higher realm) is being matched with further training. They are being made pure and clear. This is a continuous life; it has only been cut off in the eyes of the people of the earth. The people of the earth cannot see the ranks of martyrdom; they are blind from that perspective, whereas these martyrs continue to ascend the ranks of elevation in the higher world. They are attaining further divine lights in guidance, purity, radiance and clarity.... And last of all!

Surah 47, verse 6 of the Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation):

﴿And He will admit them into Paradise, which He has made known to them.﴾ (47:6)

There are narrations in the Hadith concerning the martyrs (shuhada') that they are shown their place of abode in Paradise. Imam Ahmad has related it: from Zaid ibn Hubab? This is the recognition by the people of Paradise of their places of abode, and this is their guidance, and this is their setting right of their condition. Leaving this world behind, they live an exceedingly elevated life.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 47, verse 7:

Those who were killed in the way of Allah, their honour, Allah's pleasure with them, their protection and the atmosphere of their lofty station, all call the believers to devote themselves wholly to Allah and to stand up in support of the Islamic system. They are promised that Allah will help them, and destruction is decreed for the enemies of Allah and for your enemies.

﴿O you who believe, if you help Allah, He will help you and make your feet firm. As for those who disbelieve, for them is destruction, and He will make their deeds go astray. That is because they disliked what Allah revealed, so He has made their deeds fruitless.﴾ (47:7-9)

How do the believers help Allah? So that they may fulfil their condition, and Allah in return may grant them victory and make them steadfast. Allah's requirement is that they become sincere to Allah and associate nothing with Him, neither overt shirk nor hidden shirk. They must not place their trust in any person or thing in opposition to Allah. Allah must become dearer to them than their own selves and all beloved things, and Allah must rule over a person's desires, inclinations, preferences, movements and stillness, his passing thoughts and all his activities. This is the help of Allah from the side of human souls.

The truth is that Allah has prescribed for human life a Shariah and a system of living, and this system has been formed upon a particular conception of this life and this universe. Allah's help takes the form of supporting His system and implementing it throughout the whole of life. This is the help of Allah in our real life.

Two phrases here are very important and deserve reflection.

The first is ﴿those who were killed in the way of Allah﴾. The second is ﴿if you help Allah﴾. In both situations, that is, in being killed and in helping, it is necessary that it be in the way of Allah. This is a very clear and noteworthy point, but when centuries pass over an idea, its original form becomes distorted. People use the words shahadah (martyrdom) and jihad very often, but their true meaning and conditions remain hidden from their eyes.

There is no jihad, no paradise, and no martyrdom, except when it is purely for Allah, in the way of Allah: one who is killed purely for Allah, dying to support the system of Allah, and who implements that system in his own self and in his way of life.

There is no jihad, no martyrdom and no paradise, unless all of it is for the elevation of the word of Allah, and so that the system of Allah may prevail in people's lives, be implemented in their morals and conduct, and in their circumstances, laws and constitution.

Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (may Allah be pleased with him) narrates that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about a man who fights for display of bravery, or fights out of tribal zeal (hamiyyah jahiliyyah), or fights for show. Are these in the way of Allah? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: whoever fights so that the word of Allah is exalted, he alone is in the way of Allah. (Bukhari, Muslim, Tirmidhi and Nasa'i)

The Islamic jihad has no other banner and no other aim. One who fights for Allah fights only for Allah. Therefore the one who is martyred is the one who is martyred for Him alone. The promise of paradise is only for such martyrs. Only this banner and this aim are accepted. Not those which, after centuries have passed, became new banners, new aims came to the fore, and new names were adopted!

The callers to truth should understand this clear matter, and should be mindful of the deviation that has occurred in our societies' conception of jihad and qital, and should correct it. For new idols and their new banners the word jihad is also used. Therefore they should keep their creed and the meaning of jihad clear and transparent.

I say again: jihad is only that which is for the elevation of the word of Allah. The elevation of the word of Allah in the human soul, the elevation of the word of Allah in the human conscience, the elevation of the word of Allah in morals and conduct, the elevation of the word of Allah in the organisation of the state and its institutions, the elevation of the word of Allah in relationships and connections, and the elevation and exaltation of the word of Allah in every turn and every aspect of life. Any slogan other than this is not Allah; it is for Satan. For any aim other than this there is neither martyrdom, nor paradise, nor the help of Allah, nor steadfastness. It is nothing but deception and fraud. Beware of the idol-worship of the modern age and of freedom.

If such a clear and pure conception of jihad and qital is difficult for other people who are not callers to Allah, then the callers to truth should purify their thoughts and their consciousness from these false conceptions. The callers of Islam should stay far from the slogans of the modern age which are not guidance in the way of Allah.

...So this is a condition from Allah upon His servants, which Allah has made obligatory. In return, Allah has made it obligatory upon Himself that He will help such servants. He will make their feet firm. This is the promise of Allah, and He never goes against His promise. If for some time the help of Allah does not appear to be coming, there are other reasons for this too. Before help and firmness of feet, it is also necessary that these exist. (For further detail, see the commentary on ﴿Indeed Allah defends﴾, the explanation of Surah al-Hajj.) It is for Allah to decide whether His servants have fulfilled the condition or not.

Now I wish that we also reflect on the words of the response to the condition: ﴿He will help you and make your feet firm﴾. First, the human mind goes to the thought that feet are made firm before help, and that after firmness help comes, and this is correct too. But here, in the mention of firmness coming after help, there is also an indication towards another state and another meaning: that when the help of Allah arrives and the believers become dominant, then the meaning of making firm is what follows. And this is a very difficult task. The struggle between faith and disbelief does not end when the help and victory of Allah arrive. The conflict between truth and falsehood continues nonetheless. The truth is that in the human self and in practical life, help has its own separate responsibilities: avoiding arrogance and pride, avoiding laziness, and avoiding wahn (weakness). Many people endure hardships, but few are able to keep their feet firm after victory and triumph. Perhaps it is this that is being pointed to here. And Allah knows best!

**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 47, verse 8:**

﴿Those who disbelieve, for them is destruction, and He has caused their deeds to go astray.﴾ This is the complete opposite of the state of victory and steadfastness. The invocation of misfortune from Allah is in fact destruction, and it is an announcement of failure and frustration. And the loss of deeds means that their deeds will be lost.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 47, verse 9:

﴿That is because they disliked what Allah has sent down, so He has made their deeds fruitless.﴾ (47:9) This presents a very vivid picture of the aversion in their hearts towards the Qur'an, and of how greatly they dislike Allah's Shari'ah and system. It is this aversion that compels them to disbelieve, to be hostile towards the Muslims, and to maintain war, conflict and disputes. In truth, this is the mental state of most people regarding Islam. They regard Islam as thoroughly repugnant and clash with it, even though it is the best and most firmly established system, yet these people do not like it. These are the kind of people found in every age and place, and you can meet them. When you meet such people, the lava of hatred against Islam will be erupting from their mouths and their conduct. Some people have such an allergy that merely mentioning Islam makes them writhe as if stung by scorpions. They strive that Islam is never mentioned in any matter or in any discussion. Many such people are found in our own age, and their conduct is no secret to anyone.

What is the punishment for such people? That Allah has rendered all their deeds null and void. The word "ḥabaṭ" (nullification, to be rendered void) used for deeds is a distinctive style of the Qur'an, in which it gives a concrete, sensory form to a meaning. The literal meaning of "ḥabaṭ" is the swelling of an animal after eating poisonous grass; by this swelling the animal dies within hours. In the same way, the deeds of the disbelievers also swell up; apparently they look very big, but their end is destruction and ruin. This is a picture, a movement, which describes the state of those who hate Islam and are proud of their great deeds, and these deeds are swollen just as an animal swells after eating poisonous grass.

After this, they are directed to look back at history and reflect. This is said with some intensity.

"Have they not travelled through the land and seen what was the end of those before them? Allah destroyed them utterly, and similar outcomes await the disbelievers." (47:10)

This is a frightening and wrathful image, full of agitation and terror. It presents the picture of people who were annihilated in the twinkling of an eye: all their traces erased, their dwellings turned into heaps of rubble, and they groaning beneath those heaps. This scene is presented in this manner, and its purpose here is precisely to be depicted thus. Through this style of expression the destruction of those nations, the transformation of their settlements into rubble, and the scale of the devastation are conveyed.

By presenting such a terrifying scene, and by displaying the destruction on the screen of words, the listeners are told that, in consequence of your attitude, a similar scene awaits you.

"And for the disbelievers there are similar outcomes" (47:10). Why do such outcomes await the disbelievers, and why is the support of the believers arranged in this way? This is the constant principle of Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 47, verse 11:

﴿That is because Allah is the Protector (Mawla) of those who believe, and the disbelievers have no protector.﴾

One whose master is Allah, and whose helper is Allah, is sufficient for him. Such a person will need no one; he will become independent of everyone. If difficult circumstances come upon such a person, he should understand that he is being tested, and that after this test there is nothing but good. This trial and these difficulties are not because Allah has abandoned him, nor because Allah is breaking His promise to help His servants. Rather, it is a trial of a believing servant. And one whose master is not Allah, his purpose is to have some other master, even if he takes all the jinn and all the humans as his masters. In the end, the one who relies on people is disappointed, even if all the forces of the world are focused on supporting him.

Now a comparison is made between the equipment of those who accepted faith and the equipment of those who disbelieved. What is the difference between these two groups who are now locked in battle with each other? And what is the difference between their equipment?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 47, verse 12:

Those who believe and do righteous deeds, [though] at times they too may eat and drink very well on this earth, yet Allah compares the portion of the believers, which is to be granted to them in the form of Paradise, with all the provisions of the disbelievers, which are to be granted to them in both this world and the Hereafter.

The portion of the believers, in terms of provision, is that there are for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, and Allah will grant them this station of honour. Therefore, the provision and the honour of the believers are very great. This is in the presence of the court of honour. This is their station with Allah, and it is based on faith, God-consciousness, and righteous action. This is in lofty Gardens, from the Lord, the Exalted, as a reward for lofty faith and superior deeds: everything is elevated!

In contrast, the provision of the disbelievers is like the grazing of cattle.

﴿وَيَأْكُلُونَ كَمَا تَأْكُلُ الْأَنْعَامُ﴾ (47:12) "They eat as cattle eat." This is their very lowly and debased condition; in it there is none of the signs of humanity. In it, it appears as though there are animals that are grazing and eating coarse, animal-like food, and in it there is no distinction between the pure and the clean, or between good and bad. Thus, this is fodder that they are eating. For it there is no code of lawful and unlawful. In it there is no matter of fear of God. Nor is there any restraint imposed by the conscience of justice.

The distinctive feature of animals is only that they eat and drink, even though animals may have developed a most refined taste in eating and drinking and made great progress in various kinds of consumer goods, as many of today's nouveau riches demonstrate. Here, this is not the point. The true human distinction is that a human being possesses a will, that there are certain standards by which he lives his life, and that he adopts what is tayyib and pure in the sight of Allah, that is, lawful sustenance. He should possess a will that is not under the pressure of human desires. Nor should his aim be before him that "Live merrily, for the world does not return again." And he should not regard this life, like cattle, merely as a dining table. And luxury and indulgence should not be life in his estimation, one that is free from the limits and restraints of lawful and unlawful. Rather, the very difference between man and animal is that man is a creature possessed of will. He has a specific purpose in this world and a specific consciousness of life, founded upon unambiguous principles, and these principles are revealed by Allah. If a person loses these matters, it is as though he has lost the station of humanity, and he remains merely an animal, because he has lost the highest of human qualities.

Now a comparison between the towns that were destroyed and the town that expelled the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

"And how many a town, which was mightier in strength than your town which has expelled you, have We destroyed, so there was none to help them" (47:13). "O Prophet (ﷺ), how many towns have passed away which were far mightier than your town that has driven you out? We destroyed them in such a way that there was no one to save them."

It is related that this verse was revealed between Makkah and Madinah when the Prophet (ﷺ) was on his journey of migration (Hijrah). In it, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is consoled, because leaving one's homeland forever is a difficult matter. The consolation is that, although these people appear to be great tyrants, obstructing the path of the Islamic call and persecuting the believers to the extent that they forced them to leave their homes while they carried the wealth of faith with them, in reality these tyrants are very weak.

﴿The likeness of the Garden which the righteous have been promised: in it are rivers of water unaltered, and rivers of milk whose taste does not change, and rivers of wine delicious to those who drink, and rivers of purified honey. This is the Qur'anic (47:15) passage.

This very vivid depiction of the pleasures of Paradise and the punishment of Hell recurs repeatedly in the Qur'an. Alongside these, at times there is also mention of purely spiritual and abstract pleasures. In several places there is also mention of pleasures in which the sensory share is small.

Allah created man. He knows man well. "Man khub mi-shanasam piran-e parsara" (I know well the elders who are pious). Allah knows, and knows most of all, what has the greatest effect on the hearts of men. How their training is possible. Which blessings are better for them and which are suitable for them. Among human beings there are those for whom, for their reform, rivers of pure water, rivers of milk whose taste is unchanged, rivers of clarified honey, and rivers of delicious wine are suitable; this is their desire. ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, the Most Merciful will endow them with affection﴾. And they will also have this certainty:

Therefore the punishment for them is also this harsh. The hottest water will be made to drink in such a way that not only will their mouths burn, but their bowels will be cut apart; and in the world these people were indeed hard like animals.
