Here this first study ends, which at the very beginning of the surah began as a critical assault on these people, and it continued in the manner that a battle continues between two camps. Until the end this struggle continued in harsh words.

Lesson No. 242 — At a Glance

This lesson concerns the hypocrites (munafiqun). It describes what their stance was regarding the person of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), what their stance was regarding the Quran, and what they thought about the obligation of jihad that had come upon the Muslims. It should be remembered that this jihad was only for raising the word of Allah. Then there are their secret relations with the Jewish tribes hostile to Islam who were spread around Madinah, and these relations were for those aims. Because of these secret conspiracies, these people wanted to uproot Islam and the Muslims from their root.

The movement of hypocrisy (nifaq) was a product of Madinah. It did not exist in Makkah, because in Makkah there were no circumstances in which anyone would need to become a hypocrite; in Makkah the Muslims were oppressed, so there was no need for anyone to become a hypocrite. When Allah honored Islam through the Aws and Khazraj in Madinah, and Islam spread among most of the families of Madinah, and most people became Muslims, then some people who did not like Muhammad (ﷺ), and did not want him and Islam to gain strength here, also became Muslims by following others. These people became Muslims, but their hearts were filled with enmity towards Islam and Muhammad (ﷺ). They sat waiting in the hope that circumstances would turn and a blow could be struck against this new power. Their leader was Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. He was the notorious hypocrite.

At the beginning of the Madinan period, the Jews in Madinah possessed a formidable military, economic and organizational strength. These people also did not like the dominance of Muhammad (ﷺ). They did not like his religion or his followers either. The presence of the Jews in this position was also a support for the hypocrites. And this common enmity soon made them one another's allies. Therefore these two forces would prepare conspiracies against the Muslims on every occasion. If the Muslims were in difficult circumstances, they would display their hypocrisy and their malice and hostility. And if the Muslims were in a good condition, they would weave a web of conspiracies against them secretly and in the dark. In the ten years of the government in Madinah, for five years they remained a great danger to Islam.

In the surahs revealed in Madinah, there is continuous mention of the conspiracies, hostilities and hypocrisy of the hypocrites. It is also mentioned that these people are allied with the Jews, take guidance from them and participate in some conspiracies. This lesson is one of them, in which a reference is made to the collaboration of the Jews and the hypocrites.

The word minhum (among them) may refer to the disbelievers, because the previous lesson was about the disbelievers, and in reality the hypocrites were also disbelievers, though they were hidden disbelievers. Allah has here counted them among the disbelievers according to their real state, that among these disbelievers some are hypocrites.

And this reference may also be to the Muslims, meaning that among the Muslims some are hypocrites, because the hypocrites regularly offered prayer and Islam, outwardly considering them Muslims, dealt with them as Muslims. But in both cases they were hypocrites. The attributes that the verse describes were in them, and this entire lesson is about them.

These people, when sitting in a gathering, appear as though they are wholly attentive and listening well, but in reality they were not listening. Rather they were fulfilling the saying "tongue in the tasbih, heart in the gaddhar" (outwardly devout, inwardly elsewhere), and even if they did listen, the matter did not reach their hearts. It is also possible that they would ask scholars mockingly, "Tell us, sir, what did he just say?" That is, nothing of it has fallen into our hands.

By this they also meant to indicate that we do not care much for these matters, while the scholars memorize every single word of the Master's sayings, both the words and their meanings. The practice of the noble Companions was also that they memorized both the words and the meanings of the sayings of the Messenger (ﷺ). And these people, that is the hypocrites, repeated these words and meanings as a jest. From all these matters it became evident that these people were extremely corrupt in nature, enemies of Islam, blind, and burned with envy at the progressing conditions of Islam.

"Ulaika alladhina ... ahwa'ahum" (47:16): "These are the people upon whose hearts Allah has set a seal, and who follow their own desires." This was the condition of the hypocrites. As for the condition of the people of guidance, it was the opposite of this.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 47, verse 17:

﴿And as for those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and grants them their taqwa.﴾ (47:17)

The sequence of events in this verse deserves attention. Those who are upon guidance take the path of guidance themselves, and then Allah grants them further guidance and bestows upon them greater depth in guidance.

﴿And grants them their taqwa﴾ (47:17). Taqwa (God-consciousness, piety) is the name of a state of the heart, as a result of which a person fears Allah at all times. He is conscious that He is watching him. One fears the wrath of Allah. He seeks the pleasure of Allah. And he guards himself from being seen by Allah in a bad state. This keen awareness is itself taqwa. Allah bestows it upon the one with whom He is pleased, and this happens when a person has an inclination to take the path of guidance. So Allah, by granting further guidance, gives him the station of taqwa. Thus, the desire for guidance, then further guidance from Allah, and then the taqwa and fear of Allah are the stages that stand in contrast to hypocrisy, heedlessness, and the following of one's desires.

Now the discussion turns to those who are hypocrites, blind and heedless, who leave the gathering of the Messenger without having benefited from what they heard. No guidance was added to them, and no fear of God arose in their hearts. Therefore they are reminded that the day of reckoning is very near.

﴿So do they await only the Hour, that it come upon them suddenly? Its signs have already come. When it does come to them, how will their reminder avail them?﴾ (47:18)

In these verses the hypocrites are awakened with a powerful jolt, and they are shaken by the collar in the manner in which one drags a person intoxicated with drunkenness. That is, these heedless people who go to the gathering of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and who return from there without taking any guidance, without remembering anything, without accepting any admonition, return empty as they were. These wretched people, what are they now preparing for?

﴿So do they await only the Hour, that it come upon them suddenly?﴾ (47:18) "Do these people await only the Hour, that it come upon them suddenly?" And their condition is that they are immersed in heedlessness and carelessness, and in wickedness and immorality.

If these people desire the Hour, then:

﴿Its signs have already come﴾ (47:18). This final messengership is the great sign of the Hour. This messengership is in fact an announcement that the Hour is about to come soon. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I and the Hour have been sent like these two," and he joined his index finger and middle finger to indicate it (agreed upon by al-Bukhari and Muslim). If to the people the time since the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) appears to be long, then the days of Allah are very long compared to our days. In the reckoning of Allah, the sign of the Hour has already come, and the greatest sign is this final messengership. And it cannot be the way of a wise person that a calamity comes and he is asleep, and then he is unable to take any measure for protection.

﴿When it does come to them, how will their reminder avail them?﴾ (47:18) This is equivalent to shaking with great force: awake, the danger is upon you; and the forceful shaking by the collar is also appropriate to the severe style of this surah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 47, verse 19:

Now the direction of address turns to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and to his companions who are guided, God-fearing, and seekers of guidance, so that they too adopt another path to guidance: acquiring knowledge and recognition (of Allah), repentance and seeking forgiveness, fear and awe of Allah, and waiting for the final hour. Allah knows well the outcome of your worldly life and your Hereafter.

﴿So know that there is no deity except Allah, and ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women. And Allah knows your movement and your resting place.﴾ (47:19) "So, O Prophet (ﷺ), know well that none is worthy of worship except Allah, and seek forgiveness for your shortcomings, and for the believing men and women. Allah knows your activities and is also aware of your dwelling places."

Here you (ﷺ) and the Muslims are directed to understand the principle upon which your community is founded, which is that there is no other deity, object of worship, or sovereign besides Allah.

﴿So know that there is no deity except Allah﴾ (47:19): "So, O Prophet (ﷺ), know well that none other than Allah is worthy of worship." Refreshing this reality in the mind, the subsequent instructions follow.

﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin﴾ (47:19): "Seek forgiveness for your shortcoming." It may be asked: were not the past and future sins of the Messenger (ﷺ) already forgiven? Yet it is the trait of a conscious, God-fearing and sensitive servant that he always regards his efforts as deficient, even if he strives greatly in obedience to Allah. The Messenger (ﷺ) knew that seeking forgiveness is itself remembrance and gratitude, and that Allah's forgiveness calls for further gratitude. Moreover, for those who would come after him in his station, and for the general Muslims, this is guidance: when the beloved of Allah is commanded to seek forgiveness although he has been forgiven, then others should seek forgiveness at all times. Also, the Messenger (ﷺ) used to seek forgiveness for himself and for the believing men and women, so that the consciousness of love for the Messenger remains fresh in the hearts of Muslims, since through the Messenger (ﷺ) they receive Allah's mercy.

And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is seeking forgiveness for the believing men and women. Then comes the final point of this series of guidance.

﴿And Allah knows your movement and your resting place﴾ (47:19): "Allah knows your activities and is also aware of your dwelling places." This brings peace to the believing heart, and it also gives rise to the awareness that Allah knows our movements as well as our end. The peace is that Allah is with us; the fear is that Allah knows us in every state, and we cannot commit disobedience secretly from Him. This is Islamic training: keep a keen awareness of Allah, always fear Him, and always remain in anticipation of what He decides.

Now the discussion turns to an extremely sensitive position. Up to this point the policy had been "hold back from jihad and fighting," but now Allah has commanded jihad. This was a blow to the hypocrites (munafiqeen). They were terrified, because now it had become difficult for them to remain hidden. They felt that if they remained in hypocrisy and did not accept Islam with sincerity, their inner state would be exposed, because when the decision for jihad is made, one must either go to battle or stay behind.

﴿And those who believe say, "Why is a surah not sent down?" But when a decisive surah is sent down and fighting is mentioned in it, you see those in whose hearts is a disease looking at you with the look of one over whom death has fallen. Better for them would be obedience and good words. But when a definite command is issued, if they had been true to Allah in their covenant, it would have been better for them. Then, can you expect anything from you but that, if you turn away, you will cause corruption in the land and sever your ties of kinship? Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, and has made deaf and blinded their sight. Do they not then reflect upon the Qur'an, or are there locks upon their hearts?﴾ (47: 20–24)

The believers were demanding the descent of a new surah, either because their hearts constantly yearned to receive new guidance, since they had immense love for the Qur'an and found in every new surah a fresh provision of knowledge and companionship. This demand could also mean that, in new circumstances, the Muslims wanted instructions and permission for jihad fi sabilillah, that they be given directives to fight and even lay down their lives for Islam.

﴿Why is a surah not sent down?﴾ (47: 20) — "why is no surah sent down (in which fighting is commanded)?"

﴿When a decisive surah is sent down﴾ (47: 20) — "in which fighting is mentioned." In it there was no room for doubt, and those who hold back from fighting, or lag behind in the works of jihad, were also condemned. Then the condition of those with diseased hearts, namely the hypocrites, began to deteriorate, and they began to draw veils behind which they plotted their conspiracies. Their wailing, lamentation, and the state of being frightened and terrified, to the point that they were overcome with fainting from fear, was worth seeing. The Qur'an here paints their picture as though they were before us on a screen.

﴿You see those in whose hearts is a disease looking at you with the look of one over whom death has fallen﴾ (47: 20). This is such a beautiful mode of expression that a person cannot imitate it, neither in another text nor in another language can one adopt this style of expression. It is such a picture of fear and dread that, beyond trembling and terror, a state of near-fainting seems to overcome these people. And in imagination, their strange and peculiar movements come before us, and all the images of those souls and personalities who have not been granted firm faith, whose nature is not true, and who do not have within them enough zeal for jihad to confront danger. These people are the sick and the hypocrites.

These people are so afflicted with humiliation, baseness, and the collapse of personality that the call to faith would need to be renewed for them from the very beginning, for faith is the true provision by which resolves become strong and by which feet become firm.

﴿Better for them would be obedience and good words. But when a definite command is issued, if they had been true to Allah in their covenant, it would have been better for them﴾ (47: 20–21). Indeed, compared with the shame in which they are afflicted, this was better for them. They are bewildered about what to do, anxious about what will happen. Now their hypocrisy cannot remain hidden, and the better policy for them now is this.

Obey and speak in a fitting manner (47:21). Now let them accept the commands of Allah wholeheartedly, rather than with hypocrisy. Let them believe in Allah and accept His commands. Let them speak words that are true, sincere from the heart, and in accordance with a firm conscience. For them, in these new circumstances, this will be more beneficial, since the commands have now become definite. Now they must either go forth to jihad or remain behind. Therefore, strive in jihad with resolve and understanding. In this way their hearts will be strengthened and their determination will become firm. Their steps will be steadfast, and jihad will not appear to them as hardship or forced labour. War will not be for them a sudden calamity whose mouth is open; they go to war so as not to fall into the mouth of that calamity. If they fight with sincere hearts, then one of the two good outcomes will certainly be theirs: either deliverance from danger and victory, or martyrdom and Paradise. And this second outcome will be better. This is the provision for the journey, that is, true faith, from which resolutions become strong, feet stand firm, and impatience and anxiety disappear, and a person attains tranquillity and steadfastness.

Now they are warned with great severity about the consequence of holding back from jihad: if they turn away from Islam, they should know what their condition was before Islam. You accepted Islam with hypocrisy; how much benefit is there in that?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 47, verse 22:

فهل عسيتم ... أرحامكم (47:22) "So what else can be expected of you, that if you turn away you will cause corruption on the earth and sever your ties of kinship?" That is, this is what is expected of you. Consider the earlier circumstances: if you turn away from Islam, you will return to your former state and cut each other's throats, and the throats of your own brothers, just as you were before Islam. After warning them about turning away from Islam, it is said: what is the real condition of these people, if they remain in their present position as it appears?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 47, verse 23:

Ulā'ika alladhīna ... abṣārahum (47:23) Afalā yatadabbarūna ... aqfāluhā (47:24): "These are the people whom Allah has cursed, making them deaf and blind. Do they not reflect upon the Qur'an, or are there locks upon their hearts?" These people remain afflicted with the disease of hypocrisy (nifāq). In truth, they are genuinely turning away from this call, into which they have outwardly entered, and they do not even believe in it. Therefore:

Fa-aṣammahum wa-a'mā abṣārahum (47:23): "Allah has made them deaf and blind." Their faculty of hearing is present, and their faculty of sight is present too, but they have rendered their ears and eyes inoperative, or they have rendered inoperative the perception that is obtained through hearing and sight. It is as though these senses are not performing their proper function.

Qur'an asks in a manner of strong rebuke:

Afalā yatadabbarūna al-Qur'ān (47:24) "Do they not reflect upon the Qur'an?" — such that the veils over their eyes would be removed, their ears would hear, the light of the Qur'an would reach them, their consciousness would be stirred, enthusiasm and fervour would arise in their hearts, ... their conscience would become sincere, and within them there would come a life illumined by the light of the Qur'an, so that they would take guidance from it.

Am 'alā qulūbin aqfāluhā (47:24) "Or are there locks upon their hearts?" These locks do not allow the light of the Qur'an to enter their hearts. Their hearts are closed in the same way that when doors are shut, a person, air or anything else cannot enter inside, nor can light enter.

The conditions of the hypocrites are still continuing. It is explained what the reasons are for their turning away after having declared faith. One reason is that they have joined a Jewish conspiracy, and have made a promise to them that whatever plot they devise, they will obey them.

Qur'an asks in a manner of strong rebuke:

Afalā yatadabbarūna al-Qur'ān (47:24) "Do they not reflect upon the Qur'an?" — such that the veils over their eyes would be removed, their ears would hear, the light of the Qur'an would reach them, their consciousness would be stirred, enthusiasm and fervour would arise in their hearts, ... their conscience would become sincere, and within them there would come a life illumined by the light of the Qur'an, so that they would take guidance from it.

Am 'alā qulūbin aqfāluhā (47:24) "Or are there locks upon their hearts?" These locks do not allow the light of the Qur'an to enter their hearts. Their hearts are closed in the same way that when doors are shut, a person, air or anything else cannot enter inside, nor can light enter.

The conditions of the hypocrites are still continuing. It is explained what the reasons are for their turning away after having declared faith. One reason is that they have joined a Jewish conspiracy, and have made a promise to them that whatever plot they devise, they will obey them.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 47, verse 26:

The Qur'an presents the act of abandoning faith after guidance has become clear in a very tangible manner, namely the act of turning back and retreating on one's heels. It mentions its causes: Satan whispered into their hearts and made this evil deed appealing to them. In this mode of expression both the outward movement, of a person walking backward on his heels, and the inward movement are visible, while these hypocrites were trying to conceal these deeds of theirs well on their own part. How Satan came to dominate them, and how he succeeded in making them apostates, although at the outset these people had already believed, the reason is this:

﴿ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ ۔۔۔۔۔ بَعْضِ الْأَمْرِ﴾ (47:26) "That is because they said to those who hated what Allah had revealed: 'We will obey you in some matters.'" The Jews were in Medina, and they were the first opponents of the revelation of the Qur'an, because they expected that the last Messenger would also be a Jew, and that prophethood would end with him. These people used to expect complete victory over the disbelievers in the time of that Messenger, and they would also frighten the disbelievers with the fact that when the Last Prophet came he would dominate the whole world, and that the whole world would be under their control. Then the kingdom of the Jews would be established. But Allah sent the last Messenger from the progeny of Abraham (peace be upon him) who were not Jews, and when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ migrated to Medina, they did not like this migration either, because as a result their remaining influence and standing also came to an end. For this reason, from the very first day these people gathered against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and began a war of secret conspiracies against him. Because, apparently, they could neither fight the Messenger ﷺ on the battlefield, nor did they have any justification for it. Thus, every person who harbored enmity towards the Messenger ﷺ joined the Jews. All the hypocrites participated in these conspiracies, and this war continued between them and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, until finally the Messenger ﷺ expelled them from the Arabian Peninsula.

These hypocrites, who became hypocrites after being guided, gave the Jews this assurance:

﴿سَنُطِيعُكُمْ فِي بَعْضِ الْأَمْرِ﴾ (47:26) "We will obey you in some matters." And the preferred view is that this assurance related to the secret conspiracies which they kept preparing against Islam and the Messenger of Allah.

﴿وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ أَسْرَارَهُمْ﴾ (47:26) "And Allah knows their secrets well." This is a most threatening remark, indeed a warning: let them plan their conspiracies, we know all of it. Nothing is hidden from the knowledge of Allah, and there is no power that can stand against the might of Allah.

This life is brief, and eventually Our army will arrive and take from them the trust of life, and then:

﴿So how will it be when the angels take their souls, striking their faces and their backs?﴾ (47:27) "Then what will their condition be when the angels take their souls and lead them away, striking their faces and their backs?"

This is an extremely frightening and humiliating scene. At the time of their death they will be helpless. They will be departing from this earth while the second life is beginning. And the start of this new life will be that the angels strike their faces with great brutality and rain blows on their backsides with cudgels. Although the moment of death is itself extremely painful, a time of fear and anguish. But since they turned their backs and fled, they are being punished on their backsides. As they sowed, so shall they reap.

This is the commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 47, verse 28:

Dhalika bi-annahum ittaba'u ... a'malahum (47:28) "That is because they followed that which angered Allah and disliked His pleasure, so He has rendered their deeds worthless."

That is, they themselves chose this outcome for themselves. They themselves adopted the way that angers Allah, namely hypocrisy (nifaq), disobedience (ma'siyah), and conspiring together with the enemies of Allah, the enemies of Allah's religion, and the enemies of Allah's Messenger. They themselves disliked Allah's good pleasure and did not strive to attain it; rather, they did what provokes Allah's displeasure and wrath. Thus Allah rendered all their deeds null (habt), those deeds in which they took pride and which they disliked, and about these deeds they used to say that they were highly skilled at them. They used to plot against the believers, and thus their schemes appeared like an inflated balloon and came like a storm, but they would end in the twinkling of an eye.

Finally, it is said that Allah is Concealing, but what you are doing, wearing the false cloak of Islam over yourselves, Allah can strip away, so turn back now.

﴿Or do those in whose hearts is a disease think that Allah will not bring forth their malice?﴾ ﴿And if We willed, We could show them to you, and you would recognize them by their faces. But you will surely recognize them by the manner of their speech.﴾ ﴿And Allah knows your deeds.﴾ ﴿And We will surely test you until We know those among you who strive and remain steadfast, and We will test your reports.﴾

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 47, verse 30:

The hypocrites had full confidence in their own skill in deception, and they generally succeeded in concealing their conspiracies from the Muslims. The Qur'an tells them that this is a very foolish way of thinking. After all, God knows everything, and Allah can expose all their secrets, and tell the Muslims how much resentment against them is filled in their hearts. Allah says:

﴿And if We willed, We would have shown them to you, and you would have recognised them by their marks.﴾ (47:30) If We willed, We could show you each one of them as an individual, so that you would recognise each of them by their signs.

This verse comes after a time when Allah had already told the Prophet ﷺ the names of some of them, but nevertheless, because of their tone, their cunning, their evasive speech, and their habit of misreasoning from the Prophet's address, you knew them.

﴿But you will surely recognise them by the tone of their speech.﴾ (47:30) The matter now rests only on the knowledge of Allah, who knows all deeds as well as their motives.

﴿And Allah knows your deeds.﴾ (47:30) Nothing remains hidden from Him. Now Allah announces a test to purify the Islamic society. This test will apply to the whole Ummah. As a result of this test, the patient and the mujahidin will separate and stand on one side, their news will become known, no doubtful person will remain in the Islamic ranks, and the hypocrites will be unable to hide their hypocrisy. They are indeed very weak people.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 47, verse 31:

"And We will surely test you until We make evident those of you who strive and are steadfast, and We will test your reports." (47:31): "We will surely test you so that We may examine your circumstances, see for ourselves, and know who among you are the mujahidin (those who strive) and the steadfast." Allah indeed knows the hidden treasures of all souls. He knows what lies beneath the earth and in the depths of the world. He knows the secret and concealed matters of human beings. And He knows what is yet to occur in the same way as if it had already taken place. Now, how does Allah wish to know the further mujahidin and sabirin (steadfast ones)?

The reality is that Allah deals with human beings only to the extent that can be done in accordance with their strength, their nature and their capacity. Human beings do not know in the way that Allah knows. Therefore, it is necessary for this knowledge and manifestation to exist for people, so that they may know who the mujahidin and sabirin are, and so that they may benefit from this knowledge and manifestation.

Whether the trial is in difficulties or in prosperity, in blessings or in hardships, in opening the hand or in straitness of livelihood, in joy or in sorrow, through such trial the hidden capacities within souls come fully into view. Through trial, the abilities of people are made manifest. Here, the knowledge of Allah means the manifestation that takes place when people are placed in tribulation, and the abilities of people rise to the surface. (For Allah this is not new knowledge; it is new for people.) And people also see it. After tribulation, the abilities of people rise to the surface. (For Allah this is not new knowledge; it is new for people.) And people also see it. The becoming known of people's qualifications after tribulation, in a form that people can comprehend, has an effect on people's consciousness and their personality, and thus the wisdom of Allah carries out its work.

However, the command of Allah is that a person should not seek trial, and should pray that Allah protect him from His trials and keep him in well-being and mercy. But if a trial does come, he should be patient, know that the wisdom of Allah is at work within it, and entrust himself fully to the will of Allah, trusting that after the trial, Allah's mercy and well-being will be bestowed.

It is narrated from the great worshipper and Sufi, Hadrat Fudayl (rah), that when this verse was recited upon him, he would weep and make this supplication: "Allahumma la tabtalina, fa-innaka in balautana fadahtana, wa hatakta astarana, wa adhabtana" ("O Allah, do not put us to trial; for if You put us to trial, You will disgrace us, expose our concealed faults, and punish us").

**Lesson 243: At a Glance**

This lesson is the final lesson of this surah. It begins with this verse:

*Inna alladhina kafaru wa saddu...* ... *lahum al-huda* (47:32): "Indeed, those who disbelieved and averted [people] from the way of Allah and opposed the Messenger after guidance had become clear to them..."

Who are these people? The more accurate view is that they are the same people addressed in the opening of this surah in the same manner, namely the polytheists of Makkah, because it is they who adopted an arrogant attitude toward the call to Islam, disputed with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and continued to turn people away from the way of Allah to the end. However, there is also the possibility that the reference is to disbelievers in general, and that this admonition includes everyone who is a disbeliever and holds this attitude, whether he is a polytheist, a Jew, or a hypocrite, whether he does so openly or secretly. Everyone is warned that they will be unable to do anything. But the first meaning is more appropriate.

In any case, in the second and final lesson, the remaining matters are addressed to the Muslims. They are called upon to continue jihad with their selves and their wealth, not to delay in this, and not to propose that a policy of peace and security be pursued further with the disbelievers, because disbelief has reached the extreme of oppression. This reconciliation should not be made on account of any expediency: not out of weakness, not out of kinship, not out of any benefit, not out of fear of financial penalty. As for financial obligation, Allah demands only as much wealth as a person is able to bear. Allah has taken into account the natural miserliness of man in this regard. It is said that if they do not fulfil the responsibilities of this call, Allah will place that responsibility upon another and raise up another community which will discharge these responsibilities in the best manner and which will understand its importance. This is an extremely frightening warning, and it is in keeping with the themes and atmosphere of this surah. At that time, among the ranks of the believers, there existed conditions for which this warning was also the best remedy, because apart from the hypocrites there were also people who were fond of comfort, whereas the majority of Muslims were devoted, sincere, brave and renowned; the reports are full of this. Since at the time of the permission to fight all kinds of people were present, and the Qur'an was training them and raising them to high ranks, this mode of expression was adopted here.

This is the decision of Allah, a most emphatic decision: a promise of Allah that will certainly come to pass, that those who disbelieved, who stood barring the path of Islam, who sat firmly in the way of truth so that this true message would not reach people, who spent their strength, their wealth and all their resources in order that Islam should not spread. Then they opposed the Messenger of Allah at every juncture. During his life they opposed him, opposed the system of life he brought, and stood in ranks opposed to his ranks; or they, after the passing of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), opposed the religion of Islam, opposed the Islamic system of life and the system of Shariah, and opposed those who adhered to the Sunnah of the Prophet (ﷺ) and the call of Islam. And they did this in a state where:

*Min ba'di ma tabayyana lahum al-huda* (47:32): "after guidance had become clear to them." They knew that this was the truth, but due to their whims and obstinacy they became blind. And interests and expediencies inclined them toward worldly benefits in preference to the benefit of the Hereafter.

This is the emphatic decision of Allah concerning these people, and this decision is certainly to be enforced, that:

*Lan yadurru Allaha shay'an* (47:32): "They will not harm Allah in the least." These people are so weak and contemptible that they cannot cause any harm to Allah at all; therefore the intent is not to negate something they could do, but rather that they cannot harm the religion of Allah, the Shariah system of Allah, or the callers of Allah. Nor can they bring about any change in the laws of nature and the order of creation of Allah, even though they may be very powerful, and even though they may have troubled some weak Muslims for a time. What will be their end?

*Wa sayuhbitu a'malahum* (47:32): "Rather, Allah will nullify their deeds." Thus all their plots will come to nothing and be annihilated, just as a sturdy ox swells up after grazing on poisonous grass and then collapses.

In this atmosphere, in which those who disbelieved, obstructed the path of Islam, and showed enmity to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the callers to the religion were warned, the Muslims themselves are also admonished to obey Allah and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and not to render their deeds void like the disbelievers.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 47, verse 33:

﴿O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and do not invalidate your deeds.﴾ (47:33)

This harsh instruction shows that within the Muslim community too there were people who were reluctant to render complete obedience, or for whom complete obedience was a little heavy, and some sacrifices seemed excessive to them. Yet at that time these sacrifices were necessary in the face of a powerful enemy who had blocked the path of Islam. These forces were attacking Islam from every side, and these Muslims had commercial, tribal and family ties with these forces. At that time, cutting off all these ties seemed difficult to them, although the demand of the Islamic call and ideology was that all these ties be severed now.

True Muslims were deeply affected by these instructions. For a moment they trembled because of these threats, and they feared at every moment that some action might come from them that would render their deeds fruitless.

Imam Ahmad, Ibn Nasr al-Marwazi narrated in Kitab al-Salah, from Abu Qudamah, from Waki', from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from Rabi' ibn Anas, and from Abu al-'Aliyah, who said: The companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) used to think that after reciting "La ilaha illa Allah," no sin is harmful, just as no deed is beneficial along with shirk. Then this verse was revealed:

﴿Obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and do not invalidate your deeds.﴾ (47:33) After this they began to fear that some sin might invalidate their other deeds.

It is narrated from Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak that Bakr ibn Ma'ruf, from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, from Nafi', and from Ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them), narrated, saying: "We, the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), used to think that all good deeds would be accepted, until the verse:

﴿Obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and do not invalidate your deeds.﴾ (47:33) was revealed. Then we thought about what it was that would invalidate our deeds, and we said: it would be the major sins (kaba'ir), the destructive sins (mujibat), and the indecencies (fawahish), until the verse was revealed:

﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He should be associated with, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills.﴾ (4:48, 4:116) When this verse was revealed, we stopped saying that, yet we feared for those who committed major sins and feared for those who committed indecencies, and we were hopeful about the fate of one who avoided them."

From these texts it is known how true Muslims took these texts. How they became anxious and alert, how they trembled and remained fearful, how they were careful lest they be caught in their grip. How they constantly thought that their lives should conform to the divine texts, and they took the divine verses with this keen sensitivity, which is why they were Muslims of that character.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 47, verse 34:

The next verse tells us what the end will be for those who oppose the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), turn away from his obedience, persist in such an attitude, and die in disbelief in this world.

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and bar [others] from the way of Allah and then die while they are disbelievers – never will Allah forgive them.﴾ (47:34)

Forgiveness has been granted a respite in this world for everyone. The door of repentance remains open to disbelievers and sinners until the agony of death begins. When the soul reaches the throat, at that very last moment, the door of repentance closes, and the opportunity is lost forever.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 47, verse 35:

The kind of verses that address the disbelievers and hypocrites in this way also call upon the Muslims themselves. These verses warn the disbelievers to make up for their shortcomings and repent before the agony of death (sakarat) begins. For the Muslims, the address of these verses is this: keep away from the causes and paths that could lead you to that end. In this verse, both the Muslims and the disbelievers are addressed, and the laxity in calling to the faith and in jihad is linked to this verse, meaning: avoid that end and do not be slack.

﴿So do not lose heart and call for peace, when you are the superior ones. Allah is with you, and He will never let your deeds go to waste.﴾ (47:35)

This is what the Muslims are being warned against. The end of those disbelievers who opposed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is placed before them, so that the Muslims fear even the thought of it. From this warning it is evident that at that time there were people among the Muslims who regarded the continuous hardships of jihad as a heavy command, and whose resolve was weak. These people wanted peace and security so that they could remain at ease away from the hardships of war. It is also possible that some of these people had kinship ties with the polytheists or joint financial dealings with them, and from this angle they preferred peace and reconciliation, because man has always remained man, and the Qur'an treats these human and natural weaknesses in its own way. Through the training that the Qur'an continued in this manner, a miraculous group came into being in the first era. Yet, despite this effort and these successes, it cannot be denied that there were weak people in the ranks of the Muslim community, especially in the early Medinan period. Accordingly, this verse points to some such weaknesses. Observe how the Qur'an dealt with people. We too should train the people of the modern age in accordance with the Qur'anic method.

﴿So do not lose heart and call for peace, when you are the superior ones. Allah is with you, and He will never let your deeds go to waste.﴾ (47:35)

Since you are the dominant ones, do not call for peace. You are superior in belief and in your outlook on life; you are superior in your relationship with God; your Master is exalted; you are superior in the system of life, the purposes of life and the goal of life; you are superior in consciousness, morality and conduct; you are superior in strength, status and the means of victory. A great power stands behind you: "Wallahu ma'akum" (Allah is with you). Indeed, Allah is with you. You are not alone; you are under the training of the Exalted and Almighty Allah, who is the Absolute Powerful. He is your helper, ever present, watching and with you. He defends you; what is the standing of your enemies when Allah is with you? Everything you spend, everything you do, and the hardships that befall you are being accounted for. Not even one of these is lost.

﴿And He will never let your deeds go to waste﴾ (47:35). Allah will not diminish your deeds in such a way that you gain no benefit from them and receive no reward for them.

Moreover, there is no justification for showing weakness and seeking peace, because Allah has decided that you are the superior ones, that He is with you, and that not an atom of your deeds will be lost; therefore you are honored, rewarded and victorious.

The first point is this: they are told what the peace and security you seek in this world are really worth. Yes, in it you will have to make some sacrifices, but in the Hereafter you will receive your full reward, and He will not ask you for your wealth.

﴿Indeed, the life of this world is but play and amusement. And if you believe and fear Allah, He will give you your rewards and will not ask you for your wealth.﴾ (47:36)

If this worldly life has no lofty and exalted purpose behind it, then it is certainly mere play and amusement. If in this world there are no sublime aims of Islam and no exalted goals of establishing the Islamic system, then there is nothing at all. The purpose of life in Islam turns this world into a field for the Hereafter, and fulfilling the rights of Allah's vicegerency in it properly is what produces good results on the Day of Resurrection. The second clause of the verse points to this.

﴿And if you believe and fear Allah, He will give you your rewards﴾ (47:36). Believing in this world and adopting taqwa (God-consciousness) is what removes it from the sphere of play and amusement, gives it a serious standing, and raises it above mere animal pleasure and luxury. The order of the world then becomes the order of the Rightly Guided Caliphate, and it becomes joined with the higher world. When the Islamic system and the law of the Shari'ah are enforced, the believer's worldly life too leaves the sphere of play and amusement and becomes an act of worship, and the believer is rewarded in the Hereafter for all his activities. Yet despite this, Allah does not demand that people spend all their wealth. Islam does not burden people with difficulty even in other obligations and duties, because Allah, the Exalted, knows well that man is by nature hasty and impatient. Therefore Allah has laid on people a burden according to their capacity. Out of mercy towards people, He has not commanded them to spend all their wealth, lest the defect in their hearts be exposed.

The Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 47, verse 37:

"If He should ask you for it and press you, you would be stingy, and He would bring out your malice." (47:37)

This verse shows how wise the commands of Allah are, and how they manifest Allah's mercy and kindness: the obligations and duties prescribed in the religion of Islam are in complete accordance with human nature, and they take into account human weaknesses and human capacity. This is because Islam is a Divine (rabbani) system of life, and it prescribes a Divine system for mankind. This system is Divine in the sense that its rules have been laid down by Allah, and it is human in the sense that it takes into account the capacity, strength and environment of man. It is Allah who created mankind, and it is Allah who prescribes a system for them, because He knows His creation well, and He is al-Latif (the Subtle) and al-Khabir (the All-Aware).

Finally, their actual circumstances are placed before them, to show that in these circumstances there is a need for spending in the way of Allah. The Qur'an, in its beautiful manner, treats the miserliness in their hearts, just as it trained them in the matter of sacrifice of life.

"Behold, you are those who are invited to spend in the way of Allah. Among you are some who are miserly, yet whoever is miserly is in truth being miserly only toward himself. Allah is Self-Sufficient, and you are the ones in need of Him. And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people, and they will not be like you" (47:38).

The Qur'an has drawn the picture of that society most beautifully, and it shows that in every society, in response to the call to spend wealth, the conduct of some people differs from that of others. Some are miserly with wealth, while others are generous. This was the same situation in the early Islamic society, which has been well recorded in the traditions (riwayat), and the Qur'an has also given details in other places. Islam presented miraculous examples in this field. People gave immense sacrifices in friendship and chivalry, but despite these examples, miserliness with wealth must have still existed; some people would have given their lives, yet found it difficult to give their wealth.

This is precisely the miserliness that the Qur'an treats in this verse.

"And whoever is miserly, is only miserly against himself" (47:38). Because those who spend in the way of Allah are in fact depositing it into their own bank. And this savings will in fact benefit them at a time when there will be no income at all: when they are raised from the earth and nothing of their possessions will be with them. Therefore, it is this earnings and savings that will be of use to them there. So, if today they are miserly in spending in this regard, they are acting against themselves. They are reducing their own savings, diminishing their own wealth, and depriving themselves.

As for Allah's demand from them to spend in the way of Allah, this too is for their own good. It is greater savings for them; their own treasury and store increase. Allah gains nothing from such wealth, nor does He need any such wealth.

Therefore, there is no justification for miserliness and stinginess. The wealth you have was also given by Him, and the reward He gives in the Hereafter will also be His favour. So what you spend is also the favour of Allah.

And finally, and as a clear statement: Allah has chosen you for His call, which is a very great kindness from Him and a great honour for you. If you do not make yourselves worthy of it and do not fulfil its responsibilities, Allah will withdraw your selection and choose another people for this task. That will be a favour of Allah upon that people, and they will value that selection!

"And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people, and they will not be like you" (47:38). For those who have tasted the sweetness of faith, this is a very frightening threat: that you will be removed and another people will be brought in your place. For the person who realises that by entrusting him with the call to Islam and the responsibility of being the best of the community, Allah has granted him a great honour, this is a very great threat. Because the one who calls people to Allah has been entrusted by Allah with a great trust. He walks upon this earth with Allah's authority and support. There is Allah's light in his being. He comes and goes, and upon him are the marks of his Master.

If someone has tasted the sweetness of faith and then it is taken away from him, only he can feel this loss; only he can feel this disgrace, who has attained access to the court of Divine greatness, been granted honour, and then been rejected, with the doors closed behind him. Indeed, the life of such people who have reached the truth, and then are removed and veils are placed before them, becomes a hell.

The truth is that faith is a very great gift. Nothing in this universe has a value equal to it. The entire wealth of human life and of the whole earth is worthless in comparison, when on one pan of the scale is faith and on the other is this whole universe.
